steps.name: Lay in the far mountains

lines.text: Let the sunset clouds and the sky dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across. Its top is about 2 1/2 in from the top edge and its bottom is about 4 1/2 in from the top edge.
The outline also runs under where the green hills and meadow, and the sunlit rim will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the sunset sky, painted already: there, only soften this paint into its edge and leave it showing.
Paints, darkest first: Mountain blue, then Far violet. The paint map shows where each goes.
Brush: 3/4 inch flat.
Keep the brush level and the strokes long, left and right; along the top of each range, follow the ups and downs of the peaks with the brush's flat edge.
It should leave flat, level bands that seem to stretch away, with slight streaks that follow the stroke.

steps.meant: Two flat ranges of mountains cross the canvas just below the gold horizon, pale violet behind and slate blue in front, with no warm light on them. Below them the canvas is bare white.

steps.name: Catch the sunset on the ridges

lines.text: Let the far blue mountains dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Rinse the brush well first. Dirty water tints every color with the last one.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across. Its top is about 2 1/2 in from the top edge and its bottom is about 3 in from the top edge.
Paint: Warm peach.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat. Load: Wiped nearly dry. Only the tip goes in the paint, and no water on the brush. It should feel dry and hard to apply.
Light pressure, skimming the surface.
It should leave feathery, broken, see-through marks that catch the canvas texture. Never a solid area.
Leave what step 4 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: It went on solid. The brush was too loaded. Fix: let it dry, then dry-brush the base color back over part of it.

steps.meant: The mountain ridges have a faint warm peach edge on the sun side; the rest of each range stays its flat blue. Below them the canvas is bare white.

steps.name: Lay in the strip of lake

lines.text: Let the far blue mountains and the sunset clouds dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is about 4 1/2 in from the top edge, and its right side is at the right edge; it's about 2 in wide and 1/2 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the green hills and meadow, and the horns' dark tips will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the sunset sky and the far blue mountains, painted already: there, only soften this paint into their edge and leave them showing.
Paint: Cream gold.
Brush: 1/4 inch flat.
Keep the brush level and the strokes long, left and right.
It should leave one flat, level strip that seems to stretch away, with slight streaks that follow the stroke.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: A short, thin, pale strip of lake shines at the right edge at the foot of the mountains. Below it the canvas is bare white.
